gloss: A figure of speech in which two words or phrases with opposing meanings are used together intentionally for effect.
A contradiction in terms.

The chemical element (symbol O) with an atomic number of 8 and relative atomic mass of 15.9994. It is a colorless and odorless gas. Sometimes called elemental oxygen to distinguish it from molecular oxygen.
Molecular oxygen (O₂), a colorless, odorless gas at room temperature.
A mixture of oxygen and other gases, administered to a patient to help them breathe.
An atom of this element.
A city and local government district in Oxfordshire, England, famous for its university.
An English habitational surname derived from the city in England.
A hamlet in Ancroft parish, Northumberland (OS grid ref NU0046).
An outer suburb of Tunstall, Stoke-on-Trent, Staffordshire (OS grid ref SJ8753).
An adult castrated male of cattle (B. taurus), especially when used as a beast of burden.
Any bovine animal (genus Bos).
A binary chemical compound of oxygen with another chemical element.
Of or pertaining to oxalic acid or its derivatives.
Of or pertaining to oxaluria.
The combination of a substance with oxygen.
A reaction in which the atoms of an element lose electrons and the oxidation state of the element increases.
To treat or infuse with oxygen.
To give (a patient) oxygen therapy.
Serving to promote uterine contractions, thus accelerating childbirth.
A hormone that stimulates contractions during labor, and then the production of milk; also plays a role in social bonding.
To combine with oxygen or otherwise make an oxide.

To become oxidized.
The tail of an ox or cow.

Any substance that oxidizes, or receives electrons from, another; in so doing, it becomes reduced.

A mixture of honey, water, and vinegar, boiled to a syrup, sometimes mixed with herbs or spices.
An addictive, semisynthetic opioid (trademark OxyContin) that is similar to morphine in effect and structure; C₁₈H₂₁NO₄.
Any of many enzymes which catalyze oxidation reactions, especially ones using molecular oxygen.
Any of a class of organic compounds, of general formula RR'C=NOH, derived from the condensation of an aldehyde (R' = H) or ketone with hydroxylamine.
A nightclub or similar venue in which patrons pay to inhale doses of gas containing concentrations of oxygen higher than in air.
A plastic or rubber mask through which oxygen may be breathed from a storage tank.

A cart designed to be drawn by an ox or oxen.
An oxidizing agent, especially one used to oxidize the fuel of a rocket or a fuel cell.
Of or pertaining to Oxford or to the University of Oxford.
Of or pertaining to an oxymoron.
